tagline: From the railroad's town to Lafayette's, between horse farms.
intro: US 62 runs south out of Midway for six miles to US 60 at Versailles, through Woodford County horse country. The byway's listing names Fawn Leap, Shadowlawn, Adena Springs, Stonewall and Land's End among the farms along the way.

Midway was the railroad's idea. In 1835 the Lexington and Ohio Railroad bought a 216-acre farm and laid out Kentucky's first railroad town on it, naming it Middleway for where it lay between Lexington and Frankfort, and named the streets for its own officials.

moments.title: Midway
moments.text: When a distillery warehouse burned in 1908, Lee's Branch ran afire for over a mile, and townspeople dipping tin cups for bourbon and water got scorched, and Martin Street beside the branch was nicknamed Tin Cup Alley.

moments.title: Versailles
moments.text: The county seat was founded in 1792 on land owned by a child, whose guardian named it after the French royal town in honor of Lafayette, and it is said here as ver-SAYLZ.
